page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized virtual server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 240 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mixed performance profile. Single-core processing is a notable strength, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations show limitations, likely due to the shared CPU allocation. The stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU score fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average range, with read-only large block speeds at 70.47 GB/sec and write speeds at 41.18 GB/sec.

This instance offers high resource density, providing a substantial memory allocation and fast NVMe storage at a lower tier of qualitative cost. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which makes it less suitable for sustained, compute-heavy multi-threaded tasks. It is well-suited for memory-intensive but CPU-bursty workloads, such as database operations, caching layers like Redis (which achieved an average 6.88 million SET operations per second), static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference using small models.
